title: Choose the visual world for wohnmohr
question: The roll assigned Platform Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Platform Board
options.lineage: Indian Railways station boards and departure indicators
options.thesis: wohnmohr as a station: four products listed like departures, each telling you exactly where to go.
options.viewport: A yellow station-name board carries the wordmark and one line; directly beneath it a departure board lists Split Biller, NicheLinq, ChargeMyAI and MyThreadPay with job, domain and status.
options.risk: Can read as a theme-park gimmick if the board is decorative instead of the actual product index.

raised.raise: One lamp colour only: amber means live, and nothing else on the page may glow.
Each product carries its own platform colour band from board row to product page to share card.
Early-access products show as arriving, with what is next, never a dead label.
Every flap motion settles into a still, readable board; reduced motion shows the settled board.

options.label: Signwriter Street
options.thesis: Each product gets its own painted shop board on one street.
options.viewport: A row of four shopfront boards, each product lettered in its own colours, the company name painted on the awning above.
options.risk: The most familiar way to say 'India' on the web; tips into kitsch without a real signwriter's hand.

options.label: Glazier's Partition
options.thesis: The company as one glazed wall: each product is a pane that lights in its own colour when you step up.
options.viewport: A full-width wall of panes; the four product panes are the largest, one statement each, with company and contact panes around them.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: four panes map to four products and pane size carries hierarchy; weaker on audience identification.
options.risk: Can feel cold and architectural instead of everyday.

options.label: Packet Rack
options.thesis: Each product is a printed packet: the promise on the front, how it works on the back.
options.viewport: A rack of four packets; each front shows what the product does, and flips to its three steps and price.
options.case: Fuses well: promise and instructions map to what it does and how it works; loses on premium feel.
options.risk: Needs real painted artwork we do not have; reads crafty if faked.

options.label: VU Meter Bridge
options.thesis: Products as identical meters read as one row.
options.viewport: A row of four meters with needles.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no audience link, and needles invent numbers we do not have.
options.kept: One signal colour reserved for a single meaning.
options.risk: Implies live metrics that do not exist.

options.label: Livery Garage
options.thesis: Each product as a racing livery that reads before any word.
options.viewport: Four cars in a garage, each in its livery.
options.case: Fuses poorly: motorsport has nothing to do with splitting bills or paying wages.
options.kept: Identity carried by a colour band across every page.

options.label: Algorave Floor
options.thesis: The site as a live code buffer.
options.case: Fuses poorly: only ChargeMyAI's developers would recognise it; the dark-neon look is the AI default.
options.kept: Show what is about to change before it changes.
options.risk: Lands exactly in the near-black neon rut.

options.label: Daylight Section
options.thesis: A day of light moving through one building.
options.viewport: One long building section lit by a moving beam.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no product maps to a room, and clarity drops.
options.kept: A still state for every motion.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A product-studio homepage done straight: plain headline, four product tiles with real screenshots.
canonCard.viewport: Short headline left, product screenshots right; four product tiles below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other product studio by design.
